evaluation.positioning_hook: A college friend group takes shelter in the wrong house and discovers the family inside is feeding on them, body and soul, while one survivor fights to escape a nightmare that keeps rewriting reality.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The core promise is clean and commercial: trapped friends, a hostile house, and escalating body-horror stakes. The audience is there, but the script's extreme violence and surreal mythology narrow the lane to genre buyers rather than broad four-quadrant play.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands early with the stranded car, the welcoming family, and the reveal that the house is a trap. The later mythology expands fast, but the central engine stays legible: survive the house or be consumed by it.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Kenzie, Bryan, Zoe, Vanny, and Drew each have distinct social energy and group chemistry, especially in the early banter and later panic. They read more as functional survival pieces than deeply singular leads, though Kenzie and Zoe get the clearest emotional traction.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script commits hard to a grotesque, mythic escalation: vampires, prophecy, soul-forms, mirror transitions, and a house that behaves like a ritual machine. That boldness gives it identity, even if the mythology sometimes outruns the emotional setup.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: Once the house closes in, the script keeps throwing new threats, rooms, and reversals at the characters. The tradeoff is that the middle becomes more episodic than cumulative, with repeated capture/escape beats and long survival stretches.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The premise feels familiar at the surface level, but the execution pushes into a stranger lane with the family cult, the blood-red transformations, and the soul-birth imagery. It is not just a haunted-house setup; it has a distinct, deranged internal logic.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The house has rules, hierarchy, rituals, and a hidden cosmology, which gives the setting story-generating texture. The final wall-reveal and prophecy language suggest a larger mythos beyond the immediate siege.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a very specific register: teen banter colliding with grotesque folk-horror and surreal body terror. The tonal identity is memorable because it refuses to stay in one mode, even when that creates whiplash.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: There are hints of a larger cosmology, family history, and spiritual hierarchy beneath the violence. The material suggests depth, but much of it is delivered through exposition and revelation rather than dramatized mystery.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The friend group has enough friction, loyalty, and romantic undercurrent to keep scenes alive, especially Kenzie/Vanny, Zoe/Bryan, and the group dynamic around Drew. The house family also creates a strong opposing ensemble with its own internal structure.

lead_characters.name: Kenzie
lead_characters.demographics: Female, early 20s, college-age friend group member.
lead_characters.hook: The emotional center of the script: observant, loyal, and increasingly decisive as the nightmare escalates. She starts as the steady social glue of the group and ends as the one person willing to weaponize the house's logic against it, even when that means becoming something monstrous herself.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Florence Pugh in Midsommar or Jodie Comer in Killing Eve — a role that moves from contained vulnerability to feral command, with a final-act transformation that asks for fear, grief, and authority in the same performance.

lead_characters.name: Bryan
lead_characters.demographics: Male, early 20s, college-age friend group member.
lead_characters.hook: The group's talkative, emotionally open pressure valve, with enough confidence to joke through danger and enough fear to crack when the house starts feeding on him. He becomes one of the script's most active survivors, carrying both romantic tension and physical endurance.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gave Caleb Landry Jones in Get Out or Justice Smith in Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom room to play charm under stress and then collapse into raw panic. It offers a young actor a full-body survival arc with emotional volatility.

lead_characters.name: Zoe
lead_characters.demographics: Female, early 20s, college-age friend group member.
lead_characters.hook: An anxious, perceptive observer whose instincts keep pulling her toward the truth even when the group wants comfort. She has the script's sharpest mix of vulnerability and defiance, and her final stretch gives her a terrifying, body-altering confrontation with the house's power.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that made Anya Taylor-Joy in The Witch or Cailee Spaeny in Priscilla so watchable — a character whose stillness, fear, and sudden resolve all register in close-up. It gives an actor a strong emotional and physical descent.

lead_characters.name: Vanny
lead_characters.demographics: Female, early 20s, college-age friend group member; queer-coded relationship with Kenzie.
lead_characters.hook: The group's social engine and emotional caretaker, always trying to keep everyone connected, even when that instinct becomes a liability. Her bond with Kenzie gives the script its most intimate relationship, and her eventual fate turns her into one of the story's most disturbing images.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gave Auli'i Cravalho in The Power or Haley Lu Richardson in The White Lotus room to be warm, funny, and then devastatingly exposed. It offers a performer a relationship-forward part that later becomes body-horror tragedy.

lead_characters.name: Drew
lead_characters.demographics: Male, early 20s, college-age friend group member.
lead_characters.hook: The most physically active of the group and the one who gets the script's longest survival gauntlet. He starts as the laid-back cook and ends as a battered, desperate escape artist whose panic becomes the engine of the second half.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gave Logan Miller in Escape Room or Dylan O'Brien in The Maze Runner franchise a chance to play resourceful panic under extreme physical punishment. It is a bruising, high-stakes survival showcase.

lead_characters.name: Sunny
lead_characters.demographics: Female, older adult, matriarch of the house family.
lead_characters.hook: The polished, unnervingly gracious face of the house's ideology, equal parts hostess, interrogator, and cult leader. She is the script's clearest human antagonist until the mythology opens wider and reveals she is only one layer of the system.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gave Toni Collette in Hereditary or Rebecca Ferguson in Doctor Sleep a chance to weaponize calm, warmth, and menace at once. It is a prestige villain part with real monologue and control energy.

lead_characters.name: Susan
lead_characters.demographics: Female, late teens to early 20s, house family member.
lead_characters.hook: The most conflicted member of the house, visibly trapped between the family's doctrine and her own revulsion. She functions as the story's moral fracture line, and her late reveal reframes the house's power structure.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gave Jessie Buckley in Men or Sophie Nélisse in Yellowjackets a chance to play innocence, dread, and complicity in the same frame. It offers a performer a volatile, ambiguous turn with real sympathy.

lead_characters.name: Sally
lead_characters.demographics: Female, older teen to young adult, house family member.
lead_characters.hook: A smiling, obedient enforcer whose friendliness is always one beat away from threat. She helps sell the house's false hospitality before revealing the violence underneath it.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor the chance to play cheerful menace, like a younger version of the unnerving social masks in Ready or Not. It is a sharp supporting villain turn.

lead_characters.name: Sissy
lead_characters.demographics: Female, older teen to young adult, house family member; twin of Sally.
lead_characters.hook: The twin counterpart to Sally, with the same polished surface but a slightly different flavor of cruelty and compliance. She helps create the house's uncanny family symmetry and gets one of the script's most memorable kill sequences.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets an actor play eerie duplication and physical precision, similar to the twin energy in Orphan or Dead Ringers. It is a vivid horror-supporting part with a strong visual identity.

lead_characters.name: Sam
lead_characters.demographics: Male, young adult, house family member.
lead_characters.hook: A younger enforcer with a smug, taunting edge and a taste for humiliation. He is less ceremonial than Sunny and more openly vicious, which makes him a useful pressure point in the violence.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor the chance to play cocky, sadistic menace in the lane of a horror-franchise henchman. It is a compact but scene-stealing antagonist part.

lead_characters.name: Jack
lead_characters.demographics: Male, older adult, house family patriarch.
lead_characters.hook: The stern, rule-enforcing father figure who gives the house its authoritarian spine. He is less verbally ornate than Sunny, but his presence makes the family feel organized, ritualized, and dangerous.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives a veteran character actor the chance to play controlled patriarchal menace, like Richard Jenkins in The Shape of Water or Michael Shannon in a darker register. It is a strong authority role with horror weight.

lead_characters.name: Salem
lead_characters.hook: The silent, physical hunter who turns the second half into a brutal chase machine. He is the most purely predatory presence in the house and the one who gives the script its longest action-horror pursuit.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives a physical performer the showcase of a mute slasher presence, like Dave Bautista in Knock at the Cabin or a more feral Michael Myers-style enforcer. It is a body-performance role with real stunt and menace value.

lead_characters.name: Tiff
lead_characters.demographics: Female, early 20s, college-age friend group member.
lead_characters.hook: The friend who is initially detached and then becomes the outside-world survivor trying to make anyone believe the nightmare happened. Her late arrival gives the ending a bleak, unresolved sting.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor a strong final-scene emotional button, similar to the survivor coda in The Descent or Hereditary. It is a smaller part, but it lands the aftermath.

casting_characteristics: twin casting for Sally and Sissy
queer relationship chemistry between Kenzie and Vanny

notable_requirements: single primary house/cabin with multiple rooms and hidden spaces

technical.vfx_details: Practical-heavy body horror with some creature/transformational work, mirror transitions, blood effects, and environment shifts between house states.
technical.sfx_needs: Extensive blood, gore, prosthetics, body-mutation effects, breakaway props, and wound continuity.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: genre-forward streaming launch or specialty theatrical horror play.

budget.note: The house can be built as a controlled primary set, but the snowbound road, forest chase, underground sewer spaces, and repeated gore/prosthetic sequences will push beyond a simple contained thriller.

casting.note: The hardest lift is Kenzie: she has to carry the emotional center, the final transformation, and the action escalation. Twin casting for Sally and Sissy plus a physically imposing Salem add specificity to the search.

development.note: The script's mythology expands from stranded-horror into prophecy, soul-forms, vampire logic, and cosmic house rules, so the buyer conversation will center on how much of that lore is essential versus overwhelming.

comp_set.title: Ready or Not
comp_set.why_it_comps: A trapped outsider versus a wealthy, ritualized family that turns hospitality into a kill room, with escalating dark-comic dread and a final-survivor push.

comp_set.title: The Invitation
comp_set.why_it_comps: The slow realization that the dinner-party welcome is a trap, with social politeness masking predatory intent.

comp_set.title: Barbarian
comp_set.why_it_comps: A house that keeps revealing deeper, stranger chambers and a premise that pivots from simple intrusion horror into grotesque mythology.

comp_set.title: The Descent
comp_set.why_it_comps: Claustrophobic survival horror with a female-forward ensemble, body punishment, and a relentless escape engine.

comp_set.title: Midsommar
comp_set.why_it_comps: A bright, ritualized community with a hidden belief system, where emotional vulnerability gets absorbed into a larger pagan logic.

audience_target.primary_audience: Horror fans who like trapped-house survival stories with a strong ensemble, grotesque mythology, and a final-girl-style escalation.
audience_target.demographics: 18-34 skew, slightly male-leaning but with strong female appeal; genre-native audience that responds to elevated body horror and cult-family menace.

budget_tier.note: A primary house set, limited cast, and contained exteriors keep it indie, but the gore, creature work, and multiple transformation sequences keep it from true microbudget territory.

types_of_buyers: indie financiers looking for contained high-concept horror
lane_fit.detail: This sits cleanly in the lane of contained, concept-forward horror with a strong visual hook and a castable ensemble. The house setting, ritual family, and body-horror escalation make it attractive to buyers who want a marketable genre package without tentpole spend.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone feature; the house mythology is vivid, but there is no clear sequel or spinoff vector with a separate character or world lane that would justify franchise planning.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The house is a trap with rules.
strengths.what_it_means: That gives the movie a clean commercial engine: every room can reveal a new threat, which is exactly what buyers want from contained horror. It will appeal to genre execs looking for a set-piece machine that can be sold in one sentence.
strengths.evidence: The family home keeps shifting into hidden rooms, ritual spaces, and a second reality, with the mirror and sewer passages turning the house into an active antagonist.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Kenzie has a real final-act turn.
strengths.what_it_means: The lead is not just a victim; she becomes the story's weapon, which raises the role's casting value and gives the film a memorable survival payoff. That is the kind of arc that attracts actors who want a transformation role, not just a scream role.
strengths.evidence: Kenzie moves from anxious group anchor to the one who chooses to fight, kill, and ultimately confront Susan in her true form.

strengths.what_it_means: The early banter and pairings create enough chemistry to make the first half feel lived-in, which helps the horror land harder once the group starts breaking apart. Buyers respond to ensembles that can generate both warmth and tension before the blood starts.
strengths.evidence: The car ride, the secret-santa setup, the teasing around Drew, and the Kenzie/Vanny and Zoe/Bryan dynamics all establish distinct social lanes.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The mythology is grotesque and ownable.
strengths.what_it_means: The vampire/porphyria/soul-form material pushes the script beyond generic home-invasion horror into a stranger, more memorable lane. That kind of weirdness can be a selling point for genre buyers who want something that feels like it has its own religion.
strengths.evidence: The book reveal, the blood-red transformations, the prophecy wall, and Susan's explanation of the house's power system.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Salem gives the movie a physical hunter.
strengths.what_it_means: A silent, relentless enforcer is a useful commercial asset because it creates a clear chase silhouette and a repeatable threat image. That helps marketing and gives the action-horror material a recognizable face.
strengths.evidence: Salem's pursuit through the house, sewer, and exterior chase sequences functions as the script's most sustained physical threat.

whats_special.headline: This is a contained, high-concept horror package with a strong house-as-antagonist engine, a castable ensemble, and a lead role that can turn into a serious actor showcase. The mythology is wild enough to stand out in the crowded elevated-horror lane, while the primary setting keeps the production in an indie-friendly zone that buyers can actually price.

items.area: The mythology swallows the human engine.
items.detail: Once the house reveal expands into vampires, porphyria, prophecy, soul-forms, and Earth-ruling cosmology, the script starts asking the audience to track a lot of rules at once. That is a real development friction point because the buyer conversation will immediately ask what the movie is emotionally, not just what it is mythologically.

items.area: Drew's long escape becomes a separate movie.
items.detail: The extended sewer, ladder, mirror, and body-destruction run gives the script a huge survival stretch, but it also pulls focus away from the ensemble and the house-family dynamic. Producers will notice that the second half is heavily weighted toward one character's ordeal, which changes the balance of the package.

The script goes deep into mutilation, dismemberment, forced eating, and body transformation, which makes the content lane clear but narrower. That is not a problem for horror buyers, but it does limit the pool to platforms and distributors comfortable with very explicit gore.

items.area: The house family is vivid but broad.
items.detail: Sunny, Jack, Sally, Sissy, Sam, and Salem all have strong functions, but several of them operate more as ritual roles than psychologically differentiated characters. That keeps the antagonist machine efficient, though it leaves some of the supporting villain slots less durable than the lead role.

issues.headline: The main friction is not concept clarity; it's overload. The script keeps escalating into a dense mythology and a very long survival gauntlet, which makes the package feel more ambitious than immediately clean for a buyer trying to price and position it fast.
